key: As rivers reach the sea, so, strong with praises, our holy songs reach him the Comprehensive.
s: Praising Indra, whom help, might and vigour attend like teams of horses, the singer turns to the songs; Sāyaṇa, on 6.36.3, reads the rivers as no longer seen apart once they enter the sea, and so every praise as becoming one with Indra.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 6.36.3, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 188373 (2019)

evidence.words: यथा स्यन्दनशीला नद्यः समुद्रमाविशन्त्याविश्य च विभक्ततया न दृश्यन्ते एवं सर्वा अपि स्तुतय इन्द्रेणैकीभवन्तीत्यर्थः
evidence.gloss: As flowing rivers enter the sea and, having entered, are no longer seen as separate, so all the praises too become one with Indra: that is the meaning.
evidence.licence: public domain text; transcription CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource)

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 6.36.3, at [476,3]). Plain sense faithful: the first half of 6.36.3 has help, manly might and vigour follow Indra as teams of horses, and the verse turns to the songs. Sāyaṇa on 6.36.3 (sa.wikisource rev 188373, dated 2019-02-01 by the MediaWiki API) says the flowing rivers enter the sea and, having entered, are not seen as separate, so all praises become one with Indra; the sentence carries exactly this and no more. Wilson (praises centre in him as rivers flow into the ocean) agrees. No Nirukta treatment of the hymn. entry-check ok.
